To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
colorectal adenomas are the precursor lesions of colorectal cancer.
the incidence of colorectal cancer is decreasing due to screening programs, and that a standardized pathology report is essential for a successful screening program.

the incidence of colorectal carcinoma is decreasing due to screening strategies, and that the pathologist should provide the gastroenterologist with the necessary information for further clinical management of colorectal lesions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the epidemiology of colorectal neoplasms, the histopathological assessment of endoscopic specimens, and the development of an evidence-based guideline for the histopathological reporting of colorectal neoplasm resection specimens.
the development of an evidence-based, standardized pathology report for colorectal adenoma specimens.
the epidemiology of adenomas, their histopathological characteristics, and the assessment of endoscopic resection samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
endoscopic resection of colorectal adenomas is a safe, reliable, and efficient method of prevention of colorectal cancer.
colorectal cancer screening has a positive impact on the incidence of colorectal cancer.
the incidence of colorectal cancer can be reduced by screening and resection of adenomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incidence of colorectal adenomas is high in the general population and the risk of progression to carcinoma is low.
a standardized and evidence-based assessment of colorectal adenomas and adenocarcinomas is essential for the success of colorectal screening programs.
a standardized pathology report for adenomas is necessary for a reliable prevention strategy of colorectal cancer, as well as a close interdisciplinary cooperation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pathologist is an important part of the screening team and has to be involved from the beginning of a screening procedure.

the histopathological evaluation of endoscopically resected specimens is a crucial part of the screening procedure and that the S3 guidelines are an excellent tool to ensure a standardized evaluation.
endoscopic resections are one of the most important specimens assessed by the pathologists, and that a well-structured pathology report is necessary for clinical management.
